parsed.unit: Unit 9: Parametric Equations, Polar Coordinates, and Vector-Valued Functions
parsed.question:
Consider the polar curve $r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$.

(a) Find the area enclosed by the curve.

(b) Find the slope of the line tangent to the graph of $r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$ at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$.

(c) For the curve $r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$, the value of $r$ is decreasing at the point where $\theta = \frac{\pi}{3}$. Find the rate of change of $\theta$ with respect to time at this instant, given that $\frac{dr}{dt} = -2\sin\theta$ at this point.
parsed.solution:
(a) $$\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}\int_{\pi/3}^{5\pi/3}\left(4 - (3 + 2\cos\theta)^2\right)d\theta$$

(b) $\frac{dr}{d\theta} = -2\sin\theta \Rightarrow \left.\frac{dr}{d\theta}\right|_{\theta=\pi/2} = -2$

$r\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 3 + 2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) = 3$

$y = r\sin\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{d\theta} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\sin\theta + r\cos\theta$

$x = r\cos\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dx}{d\theta} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\cos\theta - r\sin\theta$

$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{\theta=\pi/2} = \frac{\left.\frac{dy}{d\theta}\right|_{\theta=\pi/2}}{\left.\frac{dx}{d\theta}\right|_{\theta=\pi/2}} = \frac{-2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{-2\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)} = \frac{2}{3}$$

Alternatively:
$y = r\sin\theta = (3 + 2\cos\theta)\sin\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{d\theta} = 3\cos\theta + 2\cos^2\theta - 2\sin^2\theta$

$x = r\cos\theta = (3 + 2\cos\theta)\cos\theta \Rightarrow \frac{dx}{d\theta} = -3\sin\theta - 4\sin\theta\cos\theta$

$$\left.\frac{dy}{dx}\right|_{\theta=\pi/2} = \frac{3\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) + 2\cos^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 2\sin^2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)}{-3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) - 4\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)\cos\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)} = \frac{2}{3}$$

The slope of the line tangent to the graph of $r = 3 + 2\cos\theta$ at $\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}$ is $\frac{2}{3}$.

(c) $\frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{dr}{d\theta}\frac{d\theta}{dt} = -2\sin\theta \cdot \frac{d\theta}{dt} \Rightarrow \frac{d\theta}{dt} = \frac{dr}{dt} \cdot \frac{1}{-2\sin\theta}$

$$\left.\frac{d\theta}{dt}\right|_{\theta=\pi/3} = 3 \cdot \frac{1}{-2\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)} = \frac{3}{-\sqrt{3}} = -\sqrt{3}\text{ radians per second}$$
